institutionName: Institut d'études politiques de Paris (Sciences Po)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to live in Paris and get better at speaking French. The opportunity to study at SciencePo also sounded cool

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it's always difficult to settle into a new city and new institutions. The same goes here. Most get frustrated at things at some point, it just takes some time getting used to.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty overwhelming at first. Not a lot of help. You start to work things out by talking to staff and other students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an intro week, but I didn't take it. Heard from other people that it wasn't the best. You mostly just get dumped into it all and have to figure it out yourself - it does work out in the end, though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Set a couple of hours aside to figure all the systems out

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: My friends and I got pretty lucky on the Facebook groups "Danskere i Paris" and "Padam-Padam". It was pretty easy for us to find a flat together, but we heard from other people that it can be pretty difficult

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Expect to pay around 800€ a month. Probably more. Start searching in good time

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: SciencePo doesn't help with housing. You are on your own

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was fortunate enough to get all the courses I wanted. Therefore, everything worked out well for me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Like the Hunger Games. It's first-come, first-served. It's really stressful

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can see the courses before you register. There was also a guide that showed how you register. Otherwise none

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I needed

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare a list of all the courses you want. Start by choosing the mandatory courses (EP + DAK). Also, comparative politics at SciencesPo kinda sucks. I would look into whether it's possible to get it pre-approved in another way. Could be doable by choosing two 5 ects-courses, that involve comparative methods

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: SciencePo offers many interesting courses, especially electives! But be aware that the quality of the courses varies a lot. On BA level, you will also have courses with students younger than you (like 19). This does affect the academic level

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Varies a lot. I didn't have any hard courses, but the workload is heavier compared to UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Way more time and feedback from the professor. Overall, the teaching style reminds me more of high school. There are a few lectures like at UCPH, but not many.
UCPH also has a high focus on theories. SciencePo is more case-based

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Comparative Politics (10 ECTS)
The Euro, Migration and Climate Change: European Challenges and Opportunities (5 ECTS)
Europe’s Foreign and Security Policies (5 ECTS)
PHOTOJOURNALISM (5 ECTS)
TURKEY’S FOREIGN POLICY IN ITS GEOPOLITICAL ENVIRONMENT (5 ECTS)

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
PHOTOJOURNALISM and TURKEY’S FOREIGN POLICY IN ITS GEOPOLITICAL ENVIRONMENT!
Both are really unique and interesting. Some of the best classes I've taken

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When you have a lot of friends visiting, going out to eat every weekend can be really expensive in the long run

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Using a bike for transport is really cheap. Use Swapfiets
Eat at Crous Mabillon. So cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There are a lot of clubs, but they're hard to approach when you are on exchange.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many sports activities you can sign up for. Most of them are only 25€

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for sports. It's really cheap!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: All the museums. Go to other cities! We went to Marseille and Geneva, which were amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hinge, go on dates

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Paris is very international, so I didn't really experience anything challenging. Although not speaking French did feel like it was blocking becoming a "true" local

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Sidewalk cafes.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Visit other cities in France when you have time.
Try and make some international friends other than the other Danes who are going
Pick photojournalism as a sport

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Guerrisol has amazing second-hand / vintage

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to feel at home in a foreign city

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
Online learning agreement
Missing friends/family

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
